topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, outlines its scope, and presents the core learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer and experimental modelling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises from accumulated genetic changes and disrupted cellular differentiation within tissue architecture, alongside the challenges of modelling these three-dimensional processes in culture.

topics.label: Pathology of tumor invasion, metastasis, and benign-to-malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how benign and malignant tumors differ in local tissue invasion, metastatic potential, and stepwise pathological progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification systems
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and rules used to name and classify benign and malignant neoplasms across diverse tissue lineages.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how primary tumors and metastases cause systemic disease, tissue dysfunction, and patient death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the epidemiological distribution of cancers in human populations and compare tumor incidence and vulnerability across diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical detection, screening principles, and diagnostic modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the rationale and methodology of population screening, contrasting the diagnostic efficacy of screening programmes across different tumor sites.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reviewing the learning outcomes and providing administrative reminders for practical sessions and upcoming classes.
